group_assessment.weighting: A Coimbra group on diabetes-associated brain mitochondrial dysfunction using the WWOX phospho-Tyr33 antibody and the Zfra1-31 peptide supplied by the literature of another laboratory; it studies WWOX activation in a cell line and an animal model of type 2 diabetes, not biallelic loss of function. Weighted as primary evidence for pTyr33-WWOX in high glucose and as an unspecific pharmacological result for the peptide.

entries.proposition: Stated purpose: test whether activated WWOX (Tyr33 phosphorylation) drives high-glucose mitochondrial and neuronal damage, with Zfra1-31 described as the specific WWOX inhibitor.
entries.snippet: the therapeutic potential of Zinc finger-like protein that regulates apoptosis 31-amino-acid protein (Zfra1-31), the specific inhibitor of WWOX

entries.proposition: Design: Zfra1-31 at 20 micromolar given 3 h (early) or 24 h (late) after 25 mM glucose for 48 h; the untreated comparator is cells without peptide; no scrambled, inactive or genetic-WWOX arm is described.
entries.snippet: Cells not exposed to Zfra1-31 were also used as control cells.

entries.proposition: Total-WWOX antibody was in hand: the antibody table lists a total-WWOX reagent beside the phospho-Tyr33 reagent, yet no total-WWOX result appears in any figure.
entries.snippet: WWOX1:1000RabbitMerck Millipore (ABN413)

entries.proposition: Fractionation: lysates are split into supernatant (called cytosolic) and pellet (called membrane); no result reports WWOX or p53 in a mitochondrial or membrane fraction.
entries.snippet: The supernatants represent the cytosolic fractions and the resulting pellets the membrane fractions.

entries.proposition: Statistics: one-way ANOVA or Kruskal-Wallis on 4 to 8 assays, while the control bar of most panels is the normalising value with no variance.
entries.snippet: The statistical significance was determined using the one-way ANOVA when normal distribution was observed

entries.proposition: Animal arm, 6 months: text gives cortical pTyr33-WWOX about +20% and hippocampal twofold in GK versus control.
entries.snippet: brain cortical (~ 20%) and hippocampal (twofold) pWWOX (tyr33) levels was observed in 6-month-old GK rats
entries.anchor: Results, increased levels of activated WWOX

entries.proposition: Animal arm, 12 months: text gives a cortical decrease of about 20% from the younger GK animals and no hippocampal difference.
entries.snippet: in 12-month-old GK rats, a decrease (~ 20%) in pWWOX (tyr33) levels is observed in brain cortex
entries.anchor: Results, increased levels of activated WWOX

entries.proposition: Timing claim: pTyr33-WWOX rises about 79% at 24 h in 25 mM glucose, before the roughly 15% viability fall at 48 h, and activation precedes mitochondrial dysfunction (supplement).
entries.snippet: WWOX activation preceded mitochondrial dysfunction and the increased production of ROS (SFig. 1).
entries.anchor: Results, increased levels of activated WWOX

entries.proposition: Zfra1-31 effect on the WWOX signal: text says the peptide diminished pTyr33-WWOX by about 64% and raised viability by about 16%, without separating early and late arms.
entries.snippet: Zfra1-31 diminished (~ 64%) the levels of activated WWOX (pWWOX tyr33)
entries.anchor: Results, inhibition of WWOX activation by Zfra1-31 protects

entries.proposition: p53 and caspase 3 are said to be reduced by Zfra1-31 in both arms (34 to 47% and 21 to 50%).
entries.snippet: these alterations reduced by Zfra1-31 (~ 34 (LI)—47(EI) % and 21 (LI)—50 (EI) %, respectively)
entries.anchor: Results, inhibition of WWOX activation by Zfra1-31 protects

entries.proposition: Respirometry: text reports proton leak lowered by about 65 to 70% in both arms.
entries.snippet: normalized mitochondrial proton leak by decreasing it ~ 65–70%, respectively

entries.proposition: Oxidative damage: text reports a twofold reduction in TBARS with early Zfra1-31 and about 90% rise in carbonyls with high glucose.
entries.snippet: the EI condition promoted a twofold reduction in the levels of this lipid peroxidation marker

entries.proposition: Dynamics: Results call the Fis1 and Mfn2 rises non-significant, yet the Discussion lists a Fis1 increase as characterising the imbalance.
entries.snippet: characterized by an increase in protein levels of Fis1 and OPA-1 and a decrease in Mfn1 and pDRP1/DRP1
entries.anchor: Discussion, mitochondrial fission and fusion paragraph

entries.proposition: Biogenesis: text gives ND1 up 42% and NRF1 down about 62% with late Zfra1-31.
entries.snippet: in LI condition, Zfra1-31 significantly increased (42%) ND1 and reduced (~ 62%) NRF1 levels

entries.proposition: Neurotoxic proteins: text says high glucose gave a twofold pTau and threefold Abeta rise that Zfra1-31 normalised.
entries.snippet: high glucose promoted a twofold increase in pTau (ser396) and a threefold increase in Aβ levels
entries.anchor: Results, neurotoxic proteins and synapse integrity

entries.proposition: Mechanism claim: the pTyr33-WWOX and p53 complex is said to migrate to mitochondria and cause caspase activation, cited to earlier work; the paper itself reports p53 and caspase 3 totals only.
entries.snippet: Phosphorylated WWOX can bind to p53 in the cytosol and the complex can migrate to mitochondria

entries.proposition: Control peptide-alone effect: the Conclusions say Zfra1-31 does not affect mitochondria or cells under control conditions, but the data are not shown.
entries.snippet: does not affect mitochondria and cells function under control conditions (data not shown)

entries.proposition: Limits: the authors state that in vivo efficacy is untested and that rat brain material limited the animal arm, so the neurotoxic-protein and synaptic panels exist only in cells.
entries.snippet: we were unable to perform key experiments done in neuronal cells such as the evaluation of the levels of neurotoxic proteins and synaptic integrity markers
